title: PlayerInputBindings.cs
summary: Resolves every gameplay Input Action once and exposes them as properties, so PlayerMovement/PlayerControls never need to know action names or enable the map themselves.

notes.text: Fetches the shared 'Gameplay' action map from the static KeyBindings helper (one InputActionAsset for the whole game).
Action maps must be explicitly enabled before they start producing input — nothing else in the project calls Enable() for Gameplay.

notes.match: public InputAction Move { get; private set; }
notes.text: Every action other scripts might need, exposed read-only — callers can .ReadValue()/.IsPressed()/.WasPressedThisFrame() on these directly.
If the input actions asset failed to load, log a clear error and bail rather than throwing null-reference exceptions later.
Look up each action by name once, cached as a property for the rest of the object's life — cheap to call FindAction() once, wasteful to call it every frame.
